records.text: Hear this word that the Lord spoke against you, house of Israel, and against every tribe I brought up from Egypt’s land, saying:
Hear, hills, the Lord’s judgment, and you ravines, foundations of the earth! For the Lord has a case against His people, and He will argue it with Israel.
“My people, what have I done to you? How have I grieved you, or how have I troubled you? Answer Me!
For I brought you up from Egypt’s land and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam before you.
“You alone have I known among all the earth’s tribes; therefore I will exact judgment upon you for all your sins.”
For you are a holy people unto the Lord your God; and the Lord your God has chosen you to be unto Him a people for His own possession, above all the nations upon the face of the earth.
The Lord preferred you and chose you, not because you were more numerous than all the nations, for you are the fewest of all the nations,

but because the Lord loved you, and kept the oath which He sware unto your fathers, the Lord brought you forth with a mighty hand and with an uplifted arm, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, out of the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
And you shall know that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments, unto a thousand generations,
and repays them that hate Him to their face, to destroy them. He shall not delay with them that hate Him; He shall repay them to their face.
Will a lion roar from its thicket without prey? Will a young lion give its voice from its enclosure at all unless it has seized something?

For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
Will a bird fall upon the ground without a fowler? Will a trap be sprung upon the ground without catching something?
For a person does not know his time: like fish caught in an evil net, and birds caught in a snare, so human beings are trapped at an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
Will a trumpet sound in a city and the people not be alarmed? Will there be calamity in a city that the Lord has not done?
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,
I fashioned light and made darkness; I make peace and create calamities. I am the Lord God, who does all these things.
For the Lord God will certainly do no deed unless He reveals His discipline to His servants the prophets.
And the Lord said, “Shall I hide from Abraham My servant what I am doing?
Abraham shall surely become a great and numerous nation, and all the nations of the earth shall be blessed in him.

For I knew that he would command his sons and his household after him; and they shall keep the ways of the Lord, to do righteousness and judgment, that the Lord may bring upon Abraham all that He has spoken to him.”
And the Lord said, “The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has increased, and their sins are exceedingly great.
So I will go down and see whether they are being brought to an end according to their cry which comes to Me; and if not, that I may know.”
A lion will roar—and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken—and who will not prophesy?
And I said: I will certainly not name the Lord’s name or speak in His name again. And it became like a burning fire blazing in my bones; I am weakened on every side and cannot bear it.
Announce to the regions among the Assyrians and to Egypt’s regions: “Gather upon Samaria’s mountain and see the many astonishing things in her midst and the oppression within her!”
Hear this word, heifers of Bashan on Samaria’s mountain, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who say to their masters, “Give to us so that we may drink!”
“She did not know what would be against her,” says the Lord—those storing injustice and suffering in their regions.
Is there not fire, and a lawless person’s house storing lawless treasures, and injustice with insolence?
Will a lawless person be justified with a balance and deceptive weights in a pouch?
From these they filled their wealth with impiety; those inhabiting her spoke falsehoods, and their tongue was exalted in their mouth.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: “Tyre, your land will be desolated all around; he will bring down your strength from you, and your regions will be plundered.”
With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.
He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: “As when a shepherd snatches two legs or an earlobe from a lion’s mouth, so the sons of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be snatched out, opposite a tribe, and priests in Damascus.”
David said to Saul, “Your servant tended his father’s flock. Whenever a lion or a bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
I went after it, struck it, and pulled the sheep from its mouth. If it rose against me, I seized its throat, struck it, and killed it.
“Hear and bear witness to Jacob’s house,” says the Lord God Almighty,
Hear now the word of the Lord. The Lord said: “Rise, enter into judgment before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.”
“because on the day I exact judgment upon Israel for its impieties, I will also exact judgment upon Bethel’s altars. The altar’s horns will be demolished and fall upon the ground,
Behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the Lord’s word, while Jeroboam stood at the altar to offer sacrifice.

He called to the altar by the Lord’s word: “Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. He will sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifice upon you, and he will burn human bones upon you.”
He gave a portent that day, saying, “This is the word the Lord has spoken: Behold, the altar will split, and the fat upon it will pour out.”

When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who had called against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” Behold, the hand he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
The altar split, and the fat poured from the altar, according to the portent the man of God had given by the Lord’s word.
